note: Honesty levels, after the Verdant review: build = a gate proves it here; open = measured and reported, never asserted; some-true = reproduced from a named authority. An open claim without a query, a sample size and a seed is not a claim.

claims.statement: The world tick is deterministic: the same state, intents and tick produce the same events and digest.
Combat resolves weapons, armour, healing food, flight, reciprocal PvE/PvP and levels; death drops everything held.
Quests advance from visit/kill/collect/deliver/answer facts, complete once and survive a restart.
Guilds create, invite, join, rank, chat, promote and disband, and membership survives a restart.
Logout and death drop held objects where the character stood; a restart does not respawn them; only the two-hour reset returns objects home.
A guest cannot play before authentication; one accepted command per 250 ms is enforced on every transport.
The world is 24 connected rooms with reciprocal exits, descriptions, details and zone-bound mobiles.
The WebSocket wire protocol is RFC 6455.
claims.authority: RFC 6455

claims.statement: The browser AI accepts OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints through presets and a custom provider whose key is optional; it normalizes bare hosts, bases and full chat URLs without appending a second path, stores keys per origin rather than in one global slot, and never sends a saved key to another host. A fast mode uses four history pairs, 200 output tokens, temperature 0, a 45-second deadline, two look fallbacks and then a pause. The gate checks URL normalization, key modes, request shapes, the custom keyless request and history trimming.

The public watch layer supports owner-starred highlight clips with a copy action, two-option audience polls started and closed by the streamer, one vote per viewer with live counts and the result delivered to the AI, and an owner chat-off/chat-on toggle. Highlight text passes the same private-line filter as public text; poll and vote frames are separate from game commands; chat and votes share a 1.5-second per-connection limit. The gate covers the highlight event kind, poll/chat server paths and watch-page rendering; a live server rehearsal counted a vote, delivered the poll result and rendered a highlight.

The server accepts AberMUD-style short forms (l, x/ex, g/get/grab, dr, i/inv, eq, sc, q/j, wh, aw, h/?, gos/goss, gc/gchat, status/time) and exposes an `equipment` view with armour, wielded item and worn items. After each accepted command it sends a hidden `#state` JSON line with world reset/online/phase/weather and the actor level, XP to next, HP, quests, inventory count, guild/rank, wielded and worn items. The browser AI and harness use that state in the prompt and R4 router. The gate checks the aliases, equipment view and state layer.

Gear uses eight equipment slots (head, body, hands, feet, cloak, neck, mainhand, offhand). Wearing a second item in a slot replaces the first, a two-handed weapon clears the offhand, armour sums occupied armor values plus a temporary shield bonus, and equipment lists every slot. The smith sells head, feet, hands, offhand and two-handed gear. The gate covers wear/wield/replace and the equipment map.

Magic has six spells (spark, mend, light, shield, detect, recall), a mana pool with regeneration, a spellbook that persists on the character, `spells`, `train` and `cast` commands, and a Mages' Guild room above the Atrium with an archmage trainer. Joining requires level 3 and the guild room; training adds the spell; cast spends mana and applies damage, healing, shield, light, detect or recall. The gate covers damage, mana, healing, shield expiry, recall, training and checkpoint survival.

The Lantern Quarter adds seven connected rooms, three NPCs, four objects, three personal quests and a Mages' Guild ledger quest. The world is 40 rooms and 13 quests; the Mages' Guild has guild XP and level, and a completed guild quest adds its guildXp. The gate covers the room connections, the spellwright errand, the familiar charm reward, guild quest completion and guild XP.

Production v0.47.0 serves 40 rooms, 22 mobiles and 38 objects. The Mages' Guild is room 34 above the Atrium; the smith sells the new gear; the Lantern Quarter connects from Market Square; the world has 13 quests including the guild ledger quest. Accounts remain 104 and characters 105, and /watch, /world, /live and the AI fast mode are present.

claims.statement: Deleting a pinned Prism log now revokes the sessions issued before the reset. The identity store carries a revokedBefore watermark; verifyPrismSession refuses any session whose issue time predates it with "the session predates the account reset", and wipePlayers sets the watermark when it clears the stores. The gate covers the refusal; a fresh session after the watermark is accepted by the existing signed-session fixture.

The identity store now carries an operator block list. verifyPrismSession refuses a blocked Prism id before replay checks, the server refuses a persona whose owner is blocked, and wipePlayers blocks every Prism id that held a pin at reset time before clearing the pins. The gate covers the blocked-session refusal and the wipe block list.

Production v0.63.3 holds the reset: the two Prism ids that held pins (synther and bob) are blocked, pins remain 0 after 30 seconds, and accounts/characters remain 0 while one unauthenticated guest connection stays. The verifier refuses sessions issued before the reset and blocked ids, while a freshly minted session after the reset passes the gate. The world is 70 rooms / 32 mobiles / 63 objects, landing and watch 200.

claims.statement: The direct AI contract injects the room, exits, details, objects, NPCs, room actions, inventory names, active quest objectives and a social-aware action shortlist, but remains free-form: the model may use any legal command, including say, tell and global. Reasoning is Auto/Always/Never; Auto disables provider thinking on routine turns and allows it on first turns, director messages, low HP, repeats and every eighth turn. Ollama only sends think:true for capable models and keep_alive:-1; Gemini 2.5 uses reasoning_effort none/low; OpenAI reasoning models use reasoning_effort and max_completion_tokens. Error turns carry mode fields. The Mind pane now scrolls its actual container and chat only follows when the reader is at the bottom.

The Prism-only Gemini demo is implemented behind the server. GEMINI_API_KEY never reaches the browser; an authenticated game socket issues a 30-minute demo token; the proxy enforces per-Prism daily/minute and world-wide daily quotas, forwards only the model/messages, forces reasoning off on direct turns and low on deliberate turns, and records ai.demo latency/status. GET /api/demo reports configured/model/limits without a key. The UI shows the provider only when configured and authenticates by the game socket. A mock upstream run completed Prism login -> demo token -> proxy -> command with 5 ai.turn metrics and no browser key.

Production v0.64.0 serves the free-form direct prompt with injected room/self/quest/social context, Auto/Always/Never reasoning, and the Prism-only Gemini demo path (dormant because GEMINI_API_KEY is not configured; the provider is hidden). The production setup is 542px with Reasoning=Auto and Direct prompt on; no JS errors. Local qwen2.5:7b measured p50 5.6s (22.8s first load) because inference is hardware-bound; a mock Gemini proxy run completed five turns at 9ms. Mind-pane and chat scrolling now use their real scroll containers. A live client created one legacy test account (synther, 0 progress) after the Prism block; pins remain 0.
claims.authority: wick production v0.64.0 2026-11-18; release 44392228200; gate 44390704913; /api/demo and headless setup check; local qwen/mock runs; /health

claims.statement: AI characters now carry a persistent per-character memory in browser storage: rooms seen, commands tried, stale-result counts and unexplored exits. The memory is injected as a MEMORY block every turn. A loop guard replaces a stale observation command or a movement cycle with a fresh exit, look or wait instead of pausing; it does not override speech or combat commands. The server exposes the current room with exits/objects/details at top level and the client falls back to parsed Exits text when the state line lags. A deliberately repeating mock traversed five rooms while the guard kept the run live; the gate covers stale counts, unexplored exits, cycle detection and fresh-exit selection.

The direct action menu now includes the contents of open containers as take <item> from <container>, reducing invented take/open/search commands. The server exposes contents only while the container is open. The gate still passes the AI and item suites.

Production v0.65.1 serves persistent per-character AI memory and open-container context. A real 37-turn Gemini run recorded p50 1067ms / p95 1603ms, zero errors, and varied commands (examine, talk, movement, take, wear, search, open, look). The memory prompt showed rooms seen, tried commands, stale counts and unexplored exits; a deliberately repeating mock traversed five rooms while the loop guard kept the run live. Memory is browser-local per character, not yet the R4 integer/GCD router or a portable server store.
claims.authority: wick production v0.65.1 2026-11-19; release 44427528628; gate 44426430216; /trends; headless Gemini run; repeating-mock loop test

claims.statement: The R4 router spike is documented in docs/R4-SPIKE.md. The full prime-router server indexed 23,466 wiki sentences at ~1.1 GB, started in ~2 minutes, returned wiki noise on the first game query and took 9.0-14.5s once per-turn indexing/cache work entered the path. It fails the p95 <150ms gate, so it is not deployed. The useful prime/GCD idea is implemented natively in memory.mjs: words map to stable primes, notes are prime sets, retrieval scores shared primes with room/command boosts, and the selected notes are injected as Known: each turn. The gate recalls the plaque/Vault fact from a later query.

The R4 memory sidecar is deployed on wick as a patched prime-router service on loopback: /api/context routes and retrieves only the character-scoped notes, /api/remember appends to memory_notes.jsonl, and the journal is replayed at startup. The game server proxies r4-context/r4-remember over the authenticated socket and the browser injects R4 CONTEXT ahead of the local MEMORY block, with a 60-second circuit breaker to local memory if the sidecar is unavailable. Local end-to-end calls measured 3-62ms; wick retrieval measured 11.5ms. The 349MB cache loads in 13.6s warm; no model is downloaded or used.

Production v0.67.0 runs the R4 memory sidecar on wick and injects R4 CONTEXT into the AI prompt. A 14-turn Gemini run reached p50 917ms / p95 1205ms with zero errors, used say/talk and movement/examine/take/wear, and carried prior-room context (Market Square, The Gilded Rat) into later turns. The sidecar recorded 29 calls at p50 4ms / p95 64ms / max 239ms. Warm restart is 13.6s with no model download; the local browser memory remains the fallback.
claims.authority: wick production v0.67.0 2026-11-19; release 44439824019; gate 44438484443; /api/sysinfo; /trends; ai.r4 spans; headless Gemini run

claims.statement: AI commands are validated before send: unknown verbs/targets, search targets, already-open containers, contained items without take-from, unknown spells and safe-room attacks are rejected and repaired from the current action menu; the original attempt is remembered for the next prompt and an ai.invalid metric is recorded. The trends scorecard now reports invalid rate, loops, rooms seen, memory hits, R4 hits and per-model p50/p95/invalid/loops. A live mock repeatedly sending "search an oaken chest" produced only "search" and then moved on under the loop guard, with no server Usage errors.

Command grounding is now recorded before telemetry: invalid attempts, repair target, loop guard, memory/R4 hits and rooms seen are sent in the same ai.turn metric as the command that actually ran. The validator also accepts nouns present in the current observation when the state line lags, and repairs a take on a for-sale object to buy instead of examine. The gate covers contained items, for-sale items, observation names, search targets, already-open containers and safe-room attacks.

The deploy readiness check now waits 10s after flipping units and probes login assets plus /health for up to 50s instead of 16s. This addresses the repeated transient "login assets: false" rollback where the world was still starting; the previous release deployed cleanly on an immediate retry.
